findings.reason: the author should name eddb.py (or the zarr store owner) and extend it with a record kind, or state in the section why the existing store cannot carry a grid record, so the reader does not fork placement/state ownership.
findings.text: the §7 EQDB reader declares "the record store ... beside the cache" and justifies skipping eddb.write_channel only on the array shape it stores ((channel,time) versus psi on a grid); it does not name the store owner it would extend nor show that eddb.py's zarr store (which writes an N-d data array under {shot}.zarr/{category}/{dname} with sibling arrays) cannot hold an EQDB grid record, so two stores would sit over the same JT60SA_ROOT zarr substrate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — every proposed mechanism is one deep entry point hiding its transport, store or format behind few names (RemoteEddbExtractor hides ssh+batching, eddb.py hides the cache layout, selene_deck.py the deck grammars, tokamap_export one public function, the §7 EQDB reader one remote script reusing SshTransport); §7's many touch-points are extensions of distinct existing owners, not a spread of shallow wrappers over one machine.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §7 EQDB reader forks a second record store "beside the cache" instead of naming and extending a store owner, and the stated reason (write_channel is (channel,time)) argues only against the writer, not against the zarr store substrate that eddb.py already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every remaining section that touches these families states its retirement in its own text (§2 exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §4 store-layout widening "retires nothing, because no engine has a way to see the map today", the probe-angle key "retires the machine branch"; §5 "the JT-60SA maps add files and no loader"; §6 moves eligibility into each loader's declaration, retiring the hard-coded guards; §7 EQDB reader "retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists", the machine field and second set "retire nothing, because no shot set records its machine today").
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it is about to extend and cites a verified existing owner for every mechanism it proposes: signal_map.load_packaged_signal_map, transform_engine.StoreEngine.open, description_reader.read_geometry_table, cocos_convention.score_convention, challenge/convention.measure_diiid_convention with challenge/loader.load_shot, eval/efit_referee.judge_geometry / read_efit_geometry, gs/artifact_resolution (publish_object, resolve_machine_description, PINNED_*), gs/machine_selection.ArtifactMachineSelector, spine_bench/shots.BenchShot, spine_bench/machine_artifact_arm.MachineArtifactGeometrySource, data/description_identity, and eddb_remote.SshTransport; each is opened and exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan adds a layer rather than extending, it names why: the tokamap exporter is kept out of the loaders because they read the ambix schema and must not learn tokamap's; §4's static store is a declared layout on the existing engine rather than a second engine; §6 generalises measure_diiid_convention through a loader rather than writing a second scorer; §4 supplies DescriptionSupplement/StructureAssembly as mast.json uses them.
